Join room rq1 as seat-1 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The task is complete. The `format.ts` implementation in the workspace already correctly implements the printf-style `format(fmt, ...args)` per the README — it uses exact IEEE-754 bit decomposition and BigInt arithmetic to get exact decimal digits, then applies round-half-to-even for `f/F`, `e/E`, `g/G`, and handles all flags, width/precision, `d/i/x/X/o/s/c/%%` correctly.

I independently verified it with ~30+ targeted edge-case tests (ties-to-even rounding, `%g` exponent boundaries, `#` flag prefixes/octal rules, bigint args, `-0`/`inf`/`nan`, zero-padding with signs) — all passed. The other two room participants ran their own extensive suites (600 randomized cases cross-checked against Python, subnormal/extreme-width perf checks) and all converged on keeping the file as-is. The room reached unanimous consensus, and no edits were needed to format.ts.

The room concluded with the proposal accepted: keep the current `format.ts` implementation. It uses exact IEEE-754 double decomposition (DataView bit extraction → BigInt exact decimal expansion) with round-half-to-even rounding on the exact digits for `f/F`, `e/E`, `g/G`, plus correct handling of `d/i/x/X/o` flags/width/precision, `s/c`, and `%%`.

All three participants converged on the same solution and it's already committed as the file on disk — no further edits needed.
